en.name: INR in blood
en.shortDescription: Standardised ratio derived from prothrombin time ; comparable across laboratories
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The International Normalized Ratio (INR) is a standardised, dimensionless transformation of the prothrombin time (PT) [1]. By construction, it is independent of the thromboplastin reagent used by the laboratory, which makes INR values comparable across labs — unlike PT in seconds. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a coagulation analyser on platelet poor plasma (PPP), or by a point-of-care device on capillary fingerstick blood. Results are reported as a dimensionless ratio (e.g. 2.4) [2]. **Note: relationship with PT.** The INR is derived from the PT but is *not* the same measurement. PT is reported in seconds and depends on the laboratory's reagent; INR is reported as a dimensionless ratio and is reagent-independent by construction. The data dictionary keeps them as separate concept sets ("Prothrombin time" and this set). ## Included Concepts The set is an explicit list of five LOINC "Lab Test" concepts covering INR measurements across all relevant specimens, without descendants. (LOINC 2.82 remodelled its coagulation terms (the component became the generic "Coagulation", the distinguishing part moved to the method axis) and deprecated the LOINC Hierarchy nodes this set used to be anchored on, leaving these tests under "Lab terms not yet categorized"; LOINC offers no replacement grouping.) **Platelet poor plasma**: - *3022217 / 6301-6 — INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay*: the standard hospital lab measurement. Most widely used LOINC code worldwide. - *3039326 / 52129-4 — INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --post heparin neutralization*: same numerical interpretation as the standard INR; produced when a heparinised sample is treated with polybrene/heparinase before measurement. **Whole blood**: - *3032080 / 34714-6 — INR in Blood by Coagulation assay*: INR measured on whole blood (non-capillary). **Capillary blood (point-of-care)**: - *3051593 / 46418-0 — INR in Capillary blood by Coagulation assay*: point-of-care fingerstick INR (CoaguChek and others), used for vitamin K antagonist (VKA) self-monitoring. **Specimen-agnostic**: - *3042605 / 38875-1 — INR in Platelet poor plasma or blood by Coagulation assay*: used when the source aggregates results without a specimen tag. **Note on units.** The INR is dimensionless by construction. LOINC lists `{INR}` as its example UCUM unit — an annotation-only marker carrying no dimension — but the OMOP vocabulary has no concept for `{INR}`, so the recommended unit used here is the generic **`{ratio}`** (OMOP concept 8523), already used elsewhere in this dictionary for dimensionless ratios. Source systems variously report no unit at all, `1`, `{INR}` or `INR`: all denote the same dimensionless quantity and none requires a numeric conversion. Concept 3051593 (INR in capillary blood) carries no `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` in LOINC but is given the same unit, since it measures the same quantity as the other INR concepts. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The following LOINC concepts that exist for INR-related quantities are deliberately not part of this set: - **INR goal** (`37020970 / 92891-1 — Coagulation.INR goal in Platelet poor plasma by Prothrombin time (PT)`): the *target* INR for a patient under VKA therapy, not a measurement of the actual INR. - **Reverse INR** (`3035327 / 5896-5 — Deprecated reverse INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`): a reciprocal-scale derivative used in some research contexts, not the routine INR (deprecated in LOINC). - **Fetus** specimens (`40763950 / 61189-7 — INR in Platelet poor plasma from Fetus by Coagulation assay`): out of scope for routine adult/paediatric care. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "INR", "International Normalized Ratio", "ratio normalisé international" without further specification: `3022217 / 6301-6 — INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`. By far the most common LOINC code (routine hospital lab on citrated plasma). - **Point-of-care INR** (CoaguChek, fingerstick): map to `3051593 / 46418-0 — INR in Capillary blood by Coagulation assay`. - **Specimen unspecified**: map to `3042605 / 38875-1 — INR in Platelet poor plasma or blood by Coagulation assay`. - **Whole blood** (non-capillary): map to `3032080 / 34714-6 — INR in Blood by Coagulation assay`. - **Heparinised sample treated for INR measurement**: map to `3039326 / 52129-4 — INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --post heparin neutralization`. The result is equivalent to a standard INR. - **Do not confuse with**: prothrombin time in seconds (separate concept set), or the French "TP" (taux de prothrombine), reported in % — TP is a different transformation of the PT and must never be mapped to INR. ## References [1] World Health Organization. Guidelines for thromboplastins and plasma used to control oral anticoagulant therapy. WHO Technical Report Series, No. 889, Annex 3, 1999. Available: https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/who-trs-889-annex-3 [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message:
Vocabulary update: re-resolved against OMOP vocabulary v5.0 29-AUG-26 (previously v5.0 27-FEB-26).

LOINC 2.82 remodelled its coagulation terms (generic component "Coagulation", the distinguishing part moved to the method axis) and deprecated the LOINC Hierarchy nodes this set was anchored on, leaving every test under "Lab terms not yet categorized" with no replacement grouping (confirmed in LOINC 2.83). The expression is now an explicit list of the same LOINC concepts, without descendants. Resolved concepts are unchanged.

**Renamed (1) by the vocabulary:**

- INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --post heparin neutralization → INR post heparin neutralization in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay (3039326)
